sentences.text: Petitioners are aggrieved of the impugned FIR, primarily on the ground of false implication.

The case set out by the petitioners is that petitioner No. 2 and Sadia Nawaz, daughter of respondent No.
3 eloped, contracted Nikah and executed marriage agreement on 16.03.2022.
Respondent No. 3 was against this marriage.

On 21.03.2022, when after the performance of marriage, the couple, i.e.,
petitioner No. 2 and his wife-daughter of respondent No. 3 went to Rajouri, they were arrested by Police Station, Manjakote, girl was handed over to respondent No. 3 and petitioner No. 2 was kept in the lock up.

It is case of the petitioners that respondent No. 3 pressurized petitioner No. 2 to divorce his daughter and since petitioner No. 2 did not succumb to the pressure, the impugned FIR came to be lodged.
05.

It is by far a trite and settled position of law that inherent jurisdiction vested in the High Court under Section 482 Cr.P.C. is to be exercised sparingly and with circumspection only to prevent the abuse of the process of Court or to otherwise secure the ends of justice.

It is also well settled in law that if FIR prima facie discloses the commission of a cognizable offence, the High Court in exercise of its inherent jurisdiction, shall be loathe to exercise its inherent jurisdiction.

06. As factual narration of the present case, from the status report filed, by the official respondents would unfurl, the allegation is that petitioner No. 2-Karamat c/w Hussain with the connivance of rest of petitioners hatched a criminal conspiracy and kidnapped daughter of respondent No. 3.
During investigation, the abductee- daughter of respondent No. 3 came to be recovered and she revealed that during the night of 9th and 10th of June, 2022, she was raped by petitioner No. 2.

The Investigating Officer has already obtained medical report of the prosecutrix and her date of birth certificate, according to which the victim at the time of occurrence was 14 years and three months old.
Statement of victim in terms of under Section 164 Cr.P.C. has also been recorded.

Offences under Sections 376 IPC and 4 POCSO have been added against petitioner No. 2.
07.
Mr. Bhanu Jasrotia, learned GA has produced a copy of detailed status report dated 06.12.2024.
Same is taken on record.
As per the said report, investigation of the present case is complete in all respects and final report in this respect is contemplated to be laid before the Competent Court.
08. Since the status report prima facie discloses the commission of cognizable offences against the petitioners, the present petition is found bereft of merit, hence dismissed.
09. All interim orders shall stand vacated and Investigating Agency shall be at liberty to present final report before the Competent Court of law.

(RAJESH SEKHRI) JUDGE Jammu:
11.12.2024
